title: Present perfect simple, present perfect continuous
subtitle: Results now, unfinished time, and actions that continue up to now

rows.use: Situations that started in the past and are still true
rows.example: Mrs Jenkins **has been** the head teacher for three years.

rows.use: Completed actions at a time in the past which is not mentioned
Completed actions where the important thing is the result now

blocks.intro: The present perfect simple is often used with these words and phrases:
items: {pill:for} — She's taught German here **for** five years.
{pill:since} — Mr Gray has taught French here **since** 2006.
{pill:never} — I've **never** understood why they give us so much homework!
{pill:it's the first time} — It's the **first time** we've watched a video in class.

blocks.text: We don't use the present perfect simple when we want to say **when** something happened in the past. We use the past simple.

blocks.incorrect: I **have done** my homework last night.

blocks.text: We don't use the past simple when we want to show that something happened **before now** or is **still important now**. We use the present perfect simple.
blocks.note: I've **finished**! Can I go home now?

rows.use: Actions continuing up to now or just before now
rows.example: We've **been doing** grammar exercises for over an hour. Can we have a break now?

blocks.intro: The present perfect continuous is often used with these words and phrases:
items: {pill:for} — I've been learning English **for** over three years.
{pill:just} — I've **just** been reading the school newspaper.

blocks.text: The present perfect simple often emphasises the **result** of an action.
blocks.note: She's **written** an article for the school newspaper. (= She's finished it.)

blocks.text: The present perfect continuous often emphasises the **action** and the time spent on it, rather than the result.
blocks.note: She's **been writing** an article for the school newspaper. (= She's started, but she hasn't finished it yet.)

exercises.title: A · Present perfect simple
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct present perfect simple form of the verbs in brackets.

items.prompt: I ___ this film already. (see)
John and Julie ___ their car for about a year. (have)
She ___ her driving test yet. (not / take)
Sue ___ a tour guide since she left university. (be)
___ into town on your new bike yet? (you / ride)
This new computer ___ my life a lot easier. (make)
We ___ what to get Mark for his birthday yet. (not / decide)
___ a famous person? (Paul / ever / meet)

exercises.title: C · Classroom picture
exercises.instruction: Use the prompts to write a sentence in the present perfect simple.

items.prompt: the lesson / not / start / yet
acceptedAnswers: The lesson has not started yet.
The lesson has not started yet

items.prompt: the teacher / already / write / on the board
acceptedAnswers: The teacher has already written on the board.
The teacher has already written on the board
The teacher's already written on the board.

items.prompt: Joe and Tim / just / come / into the classroom
acceptedAnswers: Joe and Tim have just come into the classroom.
Joe and Tim have just come into the classroom
Joe and Tim have just come into the classroom.

exercises.title: D · Conversation
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct present perfect continuous form of the verbs in brackets. Use short forms where possible.

items.prompt: Mandy: Hi Matt. How are you? What ___ recently? (you / do)
Matt: Oh, hi Mandy! Well, ___ for my exams. (I / study)
Mandy: That sounds boring! ___ hard? (you / work)
Matt: Very! Basically, ___ at my desk in my bedroom for the past three weeks. (I / just / sit)
I ___ out at all. (I / not / go)
___ with Michael, my best friend, some of the time, though. (I / work)
Mandy: Well, my mum and I ___ my bedroom for the last few days. (paint)
And ___ our summer holiday. (we / also / plan)
___ at different places to see which we like best. (We / look)
Matt: ___ of having a party when I finish my exams. (I / think)
